display_name: P-19 (1RL134, П-19Ш) early-warning radar, as cabled to a PU-12M
status: First electromagnetic entry for the P-19 (22 October 2026), for a radar cabled to the battery command post (scenario post.em). The transmitter, receiver and antenna figures are the Soviet technical description's; the detection anchor is the published 160 km, which the radar equation with those figures reproduces. Internals no source gives (antenna gain, losses, clutter) are estimates labelled as such.
notes: Source ids are those of docs/SOURCES.md. The P-19 is a two-coordinate radar: it measures range and azimuth, not height (the ASPD takes the height zone from the operator).

sources.title: Радиолокационная станция П-19Ш. Техническое описание ЕИ1.001.015 ТО/с, part I (posted by veterans at rtv-pvo-gsvg.narod.ru)
sources.notes: Section 2: decimetre band; three working frequencies, retuned semi-automatically in 4 s; PPI scales 100, 200, 300 km; errors (80 %, 200 km scale) +-2000 m and +-2 deg; resolution 2500 m and 8 deg; azimuth beam 4.5 deg at half power; vertical coverage to 20 deg; horizontal polarisation; sidelobes at most 5 % in power; sensitivity 1.65e-14 W (noise factor at most 4.8); bandwidth 0.8 MHz; pulse 2-2.2 us; at least 300 kW; repetition 500 and 600 Hz; 6 and 12 rpm. Section 6.2: channel 1 beam 4 deg in elevation. Section 7.3: the front end 857 +- 30 MHz. Section 4.3.3: the 1L23-6 interrogator. Section 4: a device that finds the azimuth of an active jammer.

sources.title: П-19, Russian Wikipedia (citing rusarmy.com, 'Радиолокационные станции П-15 и П-19')
sources.notes: Instrumented range 160 km; 830-882 MHz; 310 kW; 2e-14 W; 4.5 deg; 6 and 12 s per turn; coverage to 6000 m. The same 160 km is given in operator-country press as the maximum detection range.

radars.name: P-19 early-warning radar (1RL134)

freq_hz.source: p19_to (7.3: the front end works at 857 +- 30 MHz); ru_wiki_p19 (830-882 MHz)
freq_hz.notes: The band's centre; the radar works on one of three frequencies in it.

prf_hz.notes: Unambiguous range 300 km, the largest PPI scale.

peak_power_w.source: p19_to (2: at least 300 kW); ru_wiki_p19 (310 kW)

tx_loss_db.source: estimate (a long feeder to a mast antenna on the second vehicle, p19_to 6.4)

gain_db.source: derived from p19_to (4.5 deg by 4 deg)
gain_db.notes: G = 0.6 x 4 pi / (4.5 deg x 4 deg); 0.6 is a typical reflector efficiency.

sidelobe_db.source: p19_to (2: sidelobes at most 5 % in power)

scan_period_s.source: p19_to (2: 6 and 12 rpm; 6 rpm here, as the ASPD's radar_period_s)

centre_deg.source: p19_to (2: the vertical coverage to 20 deg)

height_deg.source: p19_to (2: the vertical coverage to 20 deg)
height_deg.notes: The real coverage is lobed by the ground reflection (p19_to 6.2: in-phase and anti-phase feeding of the two reflectors); one beam spanning it stands for that.

emitter.notes: Three working frequencies, retuned semi-automatically within 4 s against active jamming (p19_to 2); the frequencies themselves are not public, so no channel list.

calibration.source: ru_wiki_p19 (160 km); derived: p19_to's 300 kW, 4.5 x 4 deg beam and 1.65e-14 W at 857 MHz give 159 km for 3 m2 with 10 dB system losses
calibration.notes: No source gives a detection range against a stated target and height. The fighter-sized 3 m2, Pd 0.5 and 5000 m (inside the 6000 m coverage) are assumptions, as for the Osa's anchor.

antenna_height_m.source: estimate (as data/command/regiment_radars.json: a mast antenna on the second vehicle)

max_range_m.notes: p19_to's PPI goes to 300 km; data/command/regiment_radars.json keeps the 250 km of the coverage model.

max_elevation_deg.source: p19_to (2: the vertical coverage to 20 deg)

range_sigma_floor_m.source: estimate (finer than p19_to's +-2000 m in 80 % on the 200 km PPI scale: the ASPD takes coordinates on its 50-100 km scales)

angle_sigma_floor_deg.source: estimate (finer than p19_to's +-2 deg in 80 % on the 200 km PPI scale)

range_resolution_m.notes: p19_to's 2500 m resolution is on the 200 km PPI scale beyond 100 km.

tracker.notes: Processing choices for the commander's take-off from the ASPD's tube, not system data.

iff.source: p19_to (4.3.3: the 1L23-6 interrogator, Kremniy-2, -2M, Parol-4, its replies on the indicators); the probability is an estimate

eccm.source: p19_to (4: a device finds the azimuth of an active jammer); the threshold is an estimate

radars.notes: Coherent (СДЦ) modes К and С exist (p19_to 4.2) and are not modelled: no mti block. The radar stands on its own at the scenario's post.radar position; its echoes and strobes go to the PU-12M's IT-45 by cable.
